To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actin polymerizing proteins and non-muscles myosin II are required for dendrite retraction during self-avoidance.
actin assembly and nonmuscle myosin are required for UNC-6/UNC-40/UNC-5 mediated dendrite retraction.

UNC-6/NETRIN triggers self-avoidance by binding to the UNC-5 receptor to activate actin assembly and nonmuscle myosin contraction, and that these two mechanisms antagonize the outgrowth effect of the DMA-1/UNC-40 receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-avoiding mechanism in the dendritic growth of the PVD neuron and how this is controlled by the diffusible guidance cue Netrin.
the self-avoiding response of the dendrites of the PVD neuron.
the molecular mechanisms that determine the size of neuronal processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the actin cytoplasmic machinery is involved in the self- avoidance response in PVD neurons.
actin assembly is required for retraction, but the precise mechanisms are still unclear.
the self-avoiding mechanism is based on a balance of actin assembly and myosin contractility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-avoiding response is mediated by UNC-34, WSP-1, UNC-73, MIG-10 and the Arp 2/3 complex and that the actin cytoplasmic contractile protein NMY-1 is necessary for the self-avoidant response
the actin cytokeleton is a key player for the regulation of dendrite growth and self-avoidance.

the self-avoiding dendrite retraction is driven by the actin polymerization and non-muscles myosin II activity, and the actin polymerizing proteins are required for the UNC-6/UNC-40 mediated self-avoidance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the actin cytokeleton is not only involved in dendritic growth but also in the retraction that is needed to maintain dendrite length.
actin assembly can drive both growth and retraction of neuronal processes and that the relative balance between these opposing effects determines dendrite length.
the balance between actin polymerization versus actomyosin contractility is critical for the self-avoidant behavior of dendrites and the length of their branches.
